correctness.rationale: The subproblem reduces after positive scaling to minimizing \(xz+\theta|z|\) on \([x-\eta,x+\eta]\), with slopes \(x-\theta\) and \(x+\theta\) on the two sides of zero. This yields the complete set-valued map explicitly. For \(\eta<2\theta\), the first crossing from \(|x|>\theta\) lands inside \((-\theta,\theta]\), after which all singleton steps move toward zero and all threshold choices enter the strict interior; finite absorption follows. At \(\eta=2\theta\), the threshold minimizer intervals contain the opposite threshold points, giving the displayed admissible cycle. For \(\eta>2\theta\), every \(c\in(\theta,\eta-\theta)\) and \(c-\eta<-\theta\) are in singleton regimes, giving a unique two-cycle. Exact-rational replay independently checks representative instances of every regime.

value.rationale: The quadratic-plus-\(\ell_1\) model is the canonical one-dimensional sparse composite objective, and \(\theta=\lambda/a\) is its natural balance scale between smooth gradient and regularizer slope. The finding gives a complete sharp phase transition for the new linearized-ball method: robust finite absorption below \(2\theta\), a tie-sensitive boundary cycle at equality, and an open family of tie-free cycles above it. This directly explains when fixed-radius normalization can or cannot preserve the finite-termination behavior of the full-objective ball oracle and is therefore a structural algorithmic boundary rather than an arbitrary slice.
